findings.title: reproduction.schema.json's disposition.state enum omits "open", the value the tool itself writes
findings.description: The `disposition` object's `state` property is `"enum": ["fixed", "refused", "escalated"]` (schema/reproduction.schema.json:65-67). But `Rounds.hunt_bank!` sets `rep["disposition"] = Dict("state" => "open")` for every REPRODUCED/EVIDENCED finding (Rounds.jl:632) and immediately validates that same `rep` against `load_schema("reproduction")` two lines later (Rounds.jl:633-634), which throws `RoundError` when validation fails. "open" is not a stray typo: `Passes.jl` treats it as the normal not-yet-disposed state throughout — `get(disp, "state", "open")` (Passes.jl:700), `Dict("state" => "open")` as the fallback when no disposition file exists yet (Passes.jl:699, 1137) — so "open" is the documented initial value of the field the schema is supposed to describe. As written, the schema cannot validate the artefact the tool actually produces at the moment a bug-hunt round confirms any REPRODUCED or EVIDENCED finding, which would abort `gbg round bank` on the ordinary, non-error path of the instrument.
findings.resolution_hint: Add "open" to schema/reproduction.schema.json's disposition.state enum (making it ["open", "fixed", "refused", "escalated"]), or, if "open" is meant to be represented by the ABSENCE of a disposition key rather than an explicit state, change Rounds.jl:632 to omit rep["disposition"] entirely until a real disposition is recorded and update every get(disp, "state", "open") fallback to match that convention consistently.

findings.title: audit-changes lane_file schema requires a self-reported verdict (CLEAN/CONCERNS) that no code path ever reads
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:340-361 (classify_lane, generic across instruments, never reads data["verdict"])
findings.description: instruments/audit-changes/schema.json's `lane_file` is the only one of the four instrument lane-file schemas that adds `"verdict"` to `required` and types it as an enum `["CLEAN", "CONCERNS"]` (lines 179, 192-197) — the analogous wrappers in check-docs, check-consistency and bug-hunt do not have this field at all. Grepping the whole `src/` tree for any read of this value (`data["verdict"]`, `"CLEAN"`, `"CONCERNS"`) turns up nothing: `Rounds.classify_lane`, the single function that consumes every instrument's `lane_file`, only reads `lane`, `findings`, `checked` and `candidates_found` (Rounds.jl:340-361). The audit's own idea of "clean" — `audit["verdict_all_clean"]` in Audit.jl:52 — is computed independently from `isempty(findings)` and the executable claims' exit codes, never cross-checked against what each lane self-reported. The schema therefore enforces the SHAPE of a field whose VALUE is inert: a lane could emit findings while self-reporting "CLEAN", or emit none while self-reporting "CONCERNS", and nothing in the tool would notice — the exact self-report-without-verification pattern RULE.INST.SELF_REPORT exists to rule out elsewhere.
findings.resolution_hint: Either wire classify_lane (or an audit-changes-specific check at bank) to cross-validate data["verdict"] against isempty(data["findings"]) and reject/flag a lane whose self-report disagrees with its own findings list, or drop the required "verdict" field from instruments/audit-changes/schema.json's lane_file if the field is genuinely vestigial.
